value.hook: Read before reviewing filesystem advisory locks, lock-wait runtime boundaries, or fallback launch budgets.
value.title: Advisory locks need account-access and async proof

sections.name: body
sections.value: PR #280 at ad27621c0f995aaf4cafcd9937257ebc84018c09: a read-only descriptor to an inactive 0644 fixture acquired exclusive flock; a second open was blocked until release. File readability can therefore grant advisory-lock denial, even without directory write permission. C33 trusts the same UID, not a different account; check ancestor traversal, ownership, modes and ACL reachability instead of assuming the state directory is 0700. Cross-UID exploitation was not demonstrated. Lock creation at control.rs:445-453 inherits umask; the credential-file mode in auth.rs does not protect its parent. A synchronous acquisition loop called by async adapter methods remains on runtime workers unless a real blocking boundary is present. Correctness peer proof delayed a 50 ms timer to 3.256 s and measured 30 fallback launches from 30 reads during backoff. Restart backoff is not a fallback launch throttle: healthy tracked observer demand is (1+3P)/0.6 launches per second while control is unavailable, before launch latency and additional callers. Distinguish static traces, isolated diagnostics, peer test receipts and live-fleet measurements. Difficulties: the dependency-free frozen checkout could not pass quick local tooling checks, and the delegated initial report omitted its proof receipts. Magic wand: structured read-only review proof with tool-unavailability and evidence attribution; require a responsiveness timer whenever synchronous acquisition enters an async path.
